cases.prompt:
# Direct arylation reaction-yield optimization

Optimize the measured yield of a direct arylation reaction over the fixed, fully crossed search space below.
This is a controlled table-lookup benchmark over 1,728 measured reactions.

The process is a palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation of an imidazole with an aryl bromide, forming a new carbon–carbon bond without prefunctionalizing the reacting carbon of the imidazole. A phosphine-ligated palladium catalyst and carboxylate base enable the coupling, whose efficiency is strongly influenced by the ligand, base, solvent, concentration, and temperature.

## Search space

Use the following five parameters with these lowercase names and values.
Concentration and temperature are discrete numeric parameters.

- `base`: `Potassium acetate`, `Potassium pivalate`, `Cesium acetate`,
  `Cesium pivalate`
- `ligand`: `BrettPhos`, `Di-tert-butylphenylphosphine`, `(t-Bu)PhCPhos`,
  `Tricyclohexylphosphine`, `PPh3`, `XPhos`, `P(2-furyl)3`,
  `Methyldiphenylphosphine`, `1268824-69-6`, `JackiePhos`,
  `SCHEMBL15068049`, `Me2PPh`
- `solvent`: `DMAc`, `Butyornitrile`, `Butyl Ester`, `p-Xylene`
- `concentration`: `0.057`, `0.1`, `0.153`
- `temperature_c`: `90`, `105`, `120`

The spelling `Butyornitrile` is intentional and must be preserved.

## Objective evaluator

Maximize the single objective `yield`, measured in percent.
A separate oracle service returns the measured value for one exact candidate.
For script-based architectures, read its base URL only from `DIRECT_ARYLATION_API_URL` and call for example:

```text
POST ${DIRECT_ARYLATION_API_URL}/v1/evaluate
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "base": "Potassium acetate",
  "ligand": "(t-Bu)PhCPhos",
  "solvent": "DMAc",
  "concentration": 0.1,
  "temperature_c": 105
}
```

The response has exactly the measured objective value, for example
`{"yield": 78.95}`.
A non-2xx response is a failed attempted evaluation.

Do not access, or search for, or reconstruct the source CSV or any other complete result table.
Do not use internet access, repository search, prior campaign results, or undocumented service endpoints to discover yields.
Do not enumerate the full search space and sort by yield.
Query the oracle only for candidates selected by the optimization workflow during this invocation.

## Campaign planning

Design the optimization campaign yourself.
Choose the campaign design, including the parameter representation or encoding, initialization strategy, batch schedule, acquisition strategy, and any supported backend, using the available optimization capabilities.
Do not assume or copy campaign settings from the source benchmark implementation.

Use exactly the attempted objective-evaluation budget stated in the benchmark result contract appended below.
Every oracle request consumes one attempt.

## Output requirements

At the end, report the best reaction conditions, best measured yield, and the numbers of successful and attempted evaluations. Also report all evaluated candidates and their statuses/objective values.

In case of the no-BO-MCP architecture, every submitted or locally recorded successful result must use a `parameter_values` object containing the exact five lowercase parameter names and an `objective_values` object containing `{"yield": <measured value>}`; and save the required local JSON artifact with one record per attempt and the standardized `parameter_values` and `objective_values` objects described above.

Final answer requirement:
- Include exactly one line in this format:

BO_MCP_CAMPAIGN_ID=<campaign_id>


For this evaluation, use the BayBE backend.
